resources.string: Reads the browser URL bar and visible YouTube ad labels

Optional. Lets RustedWax read the URL bar in Brave and Chrome so it knows exactly which site is playing and which video. While that bar names a YouTube Short, it also checks visible page labels for exact YouTube ad controls such as “Sponsored” or “Skip ad”, so promoted items can be excluded from scrobbling. Unmatched page text is not stored; a matched ad label is kept only in the local diagnostic log.\n\nThis service is restricted to those browsers by the system — it cannot see any other app. Nothing from this accessibility scan is sent anywhere. The separate video-lookup switch controls network requests made from a detected video id.
Why RustedWax asks for a YouTube sign-in

The native YouTube app never tells another app which video is playing. Inside a playlist RustedWax can work it out from the playlist itself, but for a single video — or anything played with the screen off — the only thing that names the exact video is your own watch history.

What happens if you continue:

• Google's own sign-in page opens. You sign in; RustedWax never sees your password or your second factor and cannot type into that page.

• RustedWax keeps only the resulting youtube.com session, encrypted on this device under the Android Keystore. It is never written to the log, never included in an exported log, and never sent anywhere except youtube.com.

• It reads one page — youtube.com/feed/history — and only to check whether the video you just listened to is named there. It does not read your subscriptions, your email, your Google account, or any other Google service. It never posts, likes, comments or changes anything.

• Nothing from your history is broadcast. Only the video link of a track you actually finished goes on-chain, exactly as it does today.

• You can disconnect at any time from the RustedWax settings, which wipes the stored session immediately. Revoking it at myaccount.google.com works too.

The YouTube app on this phone must be signed in to the same account and not playing in incognito. If it is not, nothing you play reaches this history — RustedWax will detect that, stop using the route, and tell you why.
Experimental: reads only the foreground YouTube Shorts player

Optional and experimental. When Monitoring and Native YouTube are both on, this separately granted service reads the foreground YouTube Shorts player structure, visible title, exact @handle, current/total seekbar and literal YouTube ad labels. It measures conservative seekbar position changes. YouTube does not always draw the seekbar — for a Short that is resumed rather than opened fresh, it draws none at all — and for those the elapsed time is inferred instead, and every such listen states how much was measured and how much inferred. Background, screen-off and lock-screen time are not counted. Picture-in-picture has no seekbar to read, so it counts only if you turn on Count picture-in-picture, which infers elapsed time from evidence outside this service and marks it inferred rather than measured.\n\nAndroid restricts this service to com.google.android.youtube. It cannot see System UI, browsers or any other app. It does not use OCR, screen capture, notifications or privileged APIs, and it never reads your YouTube history — reading watch history is a separate feature you turn on yourself, and it uses no accessibility data at all. Unmatched player text is not stored or sent anywhere. Exact-id lookup remains controlled by Look videos up.
